newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's CIOR cement firm turnover up to $43.9mln.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's CIOR cement firm turnover up to $43.9mln.

text.p: Morocco's cement firm Les Ciments de l'Oriental on Friday reported a 3.0 percent growth in turnover to 382.5 million dirhams ($43.9 million) in the first half of the year over the same period in 1995.
The company's turnover in the first half of 1995 was 371.3 million dirhams.
CIOR said these results were provisional.

The cement firm made a net profit in the first six months of this year of 29.3 million dirhams. It gave no comparative figures but, for the whole of 1995, it posted a net profit of 21.6 million dirhams, Upline Securities stockbrokers said.
It has a production capacity of 2.2 million tonnes while cement sales in 1995 reached 1.37 million tonnes, it said.
Swiss cement giant Holderbank holds 51 percent stake in CIOR after its privatisation in 1993. CIOR, Morocco's second largest cement firm, has 22 percent of the Moroccan market.

"Cement market registered an average growth of 2.1 percent in 1995... But annual domestic cement consumption remains low at 235 kgs (517 lbs) per capita. It is still below the level reached by other emerging markets," Ali Amar, a market analyst at the Casablanca-based La Vie Economique weekly.
Morocco has eight cement companies with a total production capacity of 9.85 million tonnes. Domestic cement sales range around 6.4 million tonnes per year.
One of the 46 listed stocks on the Casabalanca bourse, CIOR was traded on Thursday at 355 dirhams.
